chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Uthman ibn Isa and Zura'ah ibn Muhammad from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who dies without having performed the Hajj of Islam and without bequeathing it, while he was wealthy. He said: 'Hajj is performed for him from the solid part of his wealth; nothing else is valid.'

key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: The first obligatory Hajj performed by a Muslim
key_terms.صُلْبِ مَالِهِ: The solid part of his wealth (estate)
key_terms.يُحَجُّ عَنْهُ: Hajj is performed on his behalf

ai.seo_question: How is the obligatory Hajj performed for a wealthy person who dies without doing it or bequeathing it?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the financial priority of the Hajj obligation for a deceased, wealthy individual who neglected it during life. The term 'solid portion' (sulb al-mal) indicates that the cost is deducted directly from the principal estate before the distribution of specific bequests (fara'id), establishing it as a primary debt to God. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic view that the obligatory Hajj is a binding financial duty that survives death, ensuring the spiritual debt is settled from the heir's inheritance.
